"items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. 6	
7	Every action node should validate its registry contract before authoring:
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
11	```
12	
13	`registry get` returns the manifest at `Data.Node`. Do **not** inspect `Data` directly as if it were the node manifest.
14	
15	```json
16	{
17	  "Data": {
18	    "Node": {
19	      "nodeType": "core.action.script",
20	      "version": "1.0",
21	      "handleConfiguration": [
22	        { "position": "left", "handles": [{ "id": "input", "type": "target" }] },
23	        { "position": "right", "handles": [{ "id": "success", "type": "source" }] }
24	      ],
25	      "inputDefinition": {},
26	      "outputDefinition": {}
27	    }
28	  }
29	}
30	```
31	
32	Inspect:
33	
34	- `Data.Node.handleConfiguration` — input port name and output port name(s). Array of position groups, not a map with a top-level `handles` field.
35	- `Data.Node.inputDefinition` — required inputs.
36	- `Data.Node.outputDefinition` — downstream payloads.
37	- `Data.Node.model.serviceType` — where applicable.
38	
39	Plugin `impl.md` records what to confirm for that specific node type.

42	
43	All action nodes share this base shape on the node instance:
44	
45	```json
46	{
47	  "id": "<nodeId>",
48	  "type": "<node-type>",
49	  "typeVersion": "<version>",
50	  "display": { "label": "<Label>" },
51	  "inputs": { /* plugin-specific — see plugin impl.md */ },
52	  "outputs": {
53	    "output": {
54	      "type": "object",
55	      "description": "<plugin-specific description>",
56	      "source": "=result.response",
57	      "var": "output"
58	    },
59	    "error": {
60	      "type": "object",
61	      "description": "Error information if the action fails.",
62	      "source": "=result.Error",
63	      "var": "error"
64	    }
65	  }
66	}
67	```
68	
69	`outputs.output` documents the success payload referenced downstream as `=js:$vars.{nodeId}.output`. `outputs.error` documents the failure shape; the runtime routes to the implicit `error` port when the action faults. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
70	
71	> **For action nodes the instance `outputs` block is documentation, not the runtime contract.** What actually exposes the node's outputs as process-level `$vars.{nodeId}.output` is the matching `variables.nodes[]` entry — see [file-format.md — Node outputs](file-format.md#node-outputs). The BPMN emitter ignores the action-node instance `outputs` block at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` drives the activity-side mapping). 74

76	| --- | --- | --- |
77	| Input (target) | `input` | Every action node accepts a single input edge on `input`. |
78	| Output (success, source) | `output`, `default`, or `success` | Name varies by plugin — `registry get` is authoritative. |
79	| Output (error, source) | `error` | Implicit on every action node via `outputs.error`. |
80	
81	Some plugins add dynamic source ports (e.g., HTTP `branch-{id}` from `inputs.branches`); those are documented in the plugin's own `impl.md`.

1	# HITL QuickForm Node — Direct JSON Reference
2	
3	The agent writes the `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` node directly into the `.flow` file as JSON. **Direct JSON is the default.** A CLI opt-in is available when the user explicitly requests it, or as a fallback if direct JSON writing fails — see [CLI reference: uip maestro flow hitl add](../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/shared/cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-hitl-add).
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Step 1 — Extract the Schema Through Conversation
8	
9	Before designing the schema, ask these focused questions if the business description doesn't answer them. **Ask all missing ones in a single message — never one at a time.**
10	
11	| What you need to know | Question to ask |
12	|---|---|
13	| What the reviewer sees | "What information does the reviewer need to make their decision?" |
14	| What they fill in | "Does the reviewer need to enter any data, or just click Approve/Reject?" |
15	| What actions they take | "What are the named actions — e.g. Approve/Reject, or something domain-specific like Accept/Negotiate/Decline?" |
16	
17	**Common business descriptions → schema translations:**
18	
19	| Business description | Schema shape |
20	|---|---|
21	| "Human reviews and approves/rejects an invoice" | `inputs: [invoiceId, amount]`, `outcomes: [Approve, Reject]` |
22	| "Reviewer checks agent-drafted email before sending" | `inputs: [draftEmail, recipientName]`, `inOuts: [emailBody]`, `outcomes: [Approve, Reject]` |
23	| "Escalate to human when confidence < 0.7" | `inputs: [agentReasoning, confidenceScore]`, `outputs: [action, notes]`, `outcomes: [Retry, Skip, Escalate]` |
24	| "Human fills in missing vendor data" | `inputs: [rawExtract]`, `outputs: [vendorName, costCenter]`, `outcomes: [Submit]` |
25	| "Approve before writing to ServiceNow" | `inputs: [proposedChange, targetSystem]`, `inOuts: [finalValue]`, `outcomes: [Approve, Reject]` |
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Step 1b — Discover Upstream Variables
30	
31	Before designing input field bindings, read **both** `workflow.variables.nodes` and `workflow.variables.globals` from the `.flow` file.
32	
33	### Node outputs (`variables.nodes`)
34	
35	Each entry exposes exactly what `$vars` paths are available:
36	
37	```json
38	{ "id": "fetchInvoice.output", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "fetchInvoice", "outputId": "output" } }
39	```
40	
41	The `id` field is the `$vars` path — `fetchInvoice.output` → `$vars.fetchInvoice.output`. Nested field access appends `.fieldName` (e.g., `$vars.fetchInvoice.output.invoiceId`).
42	
43	> **Binding path key = upstream script output key, not the HITL field `id`.** The HITL field `id` identifies the form field (lowercase, used for rendering). The binding path key is the property name in the upstream script's `return` statement. These are different things. If the script returns `{ supplierName: "Acme" }` and you give the HITL field `"id": "suppliername"`, the correct binding is `vars.fetchSupplier.output.supplierName` — NOT `vars.fetchSupplier.output.suppliername`. The field `id` is irrelevant to the binding path. Always look at the upstream script source to derive the key, never at the HITL field schema you are writing.
44	
45	**outputId by node type:**
46	
47	| Node type | outputId | Access pattern |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| HTTP node | `output` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.body.{field}` |
50	| Script node | `output` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{field}` |
51	| Prior HITL node | `output`, `status` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{field}` |
52	| Agent node | `output` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.content` |
53	| Trigger (manual) | `output` | `$vars.start.output.{field}` |
54	
55	### Flow-level globals (`variables.globals`)
56	
57	Also read `workflow.variables.globals`. Each entry has an `id` that maps directly to a `$vars` reference — no node prefix, no `.output` segment:
58	
59	```json
60	{ "id": "customerName", "direction": "in", "type": "string" }
61	```
62	
63	→ HITL binding: `"vars.customerName"` (no `=js:$` prefix — HITL binding is a raw path)
64	
65	**When to use globals instead of node outputs:** When data was declared as a flow-level input variable (e.g. the trigger passes it as a named parameter via `triggerNodeId`), it lives in `globals` with `direction: "in"`. Bind directly to `vars.<globalId>` — do not add `.output` or a node prefix.
66	
67	| Source | HITL `binding` format | Expression format (other nodes) |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| Node output | `vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>` | `=js:$vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>` |
70	| Flow global (`direction: "in"`) | `vars.<globalId>` | `=js:$vars.<globalId>` |
71	
72	> **`binding` vs `variable` prefix rule:** `binding` (input/inOut fields) uses the full path starting with `vars.` because it references an existing variable path. `variable` (output/inOut fields) uses `vars.<name>` — the `vars.` prefix is required; it declares the global variable name.
73	
74	For the full variable system, see → [How $vars paths are constructed in Flow](../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/shared/variables-and-expressions.md)
75	
76	---
77	
78	## Step 2 — Design the Schema
79	
80	The node schema uses `fields[]` entries inside `inputs.schema`. Use these conceptual roles to plan the fields before writing the node JSON:
81	
82	| Role | `direction` value | Human can… | Use for |
83	|---|---|---|---|
84	| Input field | `"input"` | Read only | Context the human needs to make a decision |
85	| Output field | `"output"` | Write | Data the automation needs back |
86	| InOut field | `"inOut"` | Read + modify | Data the human can see and optionally correct |
87	
88	**Supported field types:** `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `file`
89	
90	**Design rules:**
91	- Input fields: everything the human needs to decide — IDs, amounts, context; bind to upstream node output via `binding`
92	- Output fields: only what downstream nodes actually use; set `required: true` for mandatory outputs
93	- `outcomes`: use domain-specific names (Approve/Reject, not just Submit)
94	- Keep it focused — don't add fields the automation won't use
95	
96	**Show the designed schema to the user and confirm before writing the node.**

  persona: |

    but impatient: if the agent dithers, prod it to just build something. You

    You ultimately want a UiPath Flow that routes employee expense reports to a

        send it to a manager to approve or reject, then log the outcome in a
        final script step.
      - The details the manager should SEE (pulled from the first script): the
        expense amount (a number), the submitter's name (text), the category
        (text, e.g. "Travel" or "Equipment"), and an expense ID.
      - What the manager FILLS IN: their decision (approved — yes or no), and an
        optional reason if they reject.

        reads what the manager entered).

        has to review it live, so it can't be run automatically).

    If the agent asks a clarifying question that covers several of these at
    once, answer only what they asked — do not pre-empt the rest.

  constraints:
    - "Never paste or read code. If shown code, say 'I trust you, just make it work.'"
    - "Do not mention 'HITL', 'schema', 'field', 'direction', 'outcome', 'node', 'script', or 'validate' unless the agent brings them up first."

    - "When you are satisfied that the flow is built and validated, reply with exactly <<<END>>> on its own line."

  max_turns: 18
  stop_token: "<<<END>>>"
  stop_on_criteria_pass: false
  check_criteria: end_of_dialog
  n_trials: 1
  parallel_trials: true

success_criteria:
  # Name-agnostic: any .flow the agent built must validate. The exact project
  # name is scored separately below so a working-but-misnamed flow still earns
  # most of the credit. (`**` skips dot-dirs, so .uipath/.skills flows are ignored.)
  - type: run_command
    description: "uip flow validate passes (any .flow)"
    command: "python3 -c \"import glob,subprocess,sys; flows=glob.glob('**/*.flow',recursive=True); sys.exit('no .flow file found') if not flows else sys.exit(subprocess.run(['uip','maestro','flow','validate',flows[0],'--output','json']).returncode)\""
    timeout: 60
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 3.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  # Mirrors the skills-repo check_devcon_expense_approval.py: exactly one inline
  # HITL node whose schema has an amount(number) field, captures the manager
  # decision (boolean output OR approve/reject outcomes), exposes a text reason
  # output field, wires the completed handle, and is read downstream via
  # $vars.<hitl>.output.
  - type: run_command
    description: "Flow has a correct inline HITL schema, decision capture, completed wiring, and downstream .output access"
    command: "python3 -c \"import json,glob; flows=glob.glob('**/*.flow',recursive=True); assert flows,'No flow file'; f=json.load(open(flows[0])); nodes=f['nodes']; edges=f.get('edges',[]); hitl=[n for n in nodes if str(n.get('type','')).startswith('uipath.human-in-the-loop')]; assert len(hitl)==1,'need exactly 1 HITL node'; h=hitl[0]; hid=h.get('id'); schema=h.get('inputs',{}).get('schema',{}); fields=schema.get('fields',[]); outcomes=schema.get('outcomes',[]) or []; assert fields,'HITL needs fields'; ft=lambda fl,k:(fl.get(k) or '').lower() if isinstance(fl.get(k),str) else ''; assert any((ft(x,'id')=='amount' or 'amount' in ft(x,'label')) and x.get('type')=='number' for x in fields),'amount must be a number field'; dec=[x for x in fields if x.get('direction') in ('output','inOut') and any(k in ft(x,'id') for k in ('approval','approved','decision'))]; onames={str(o.get('name') or o.get('id') or '').lower() for o in outcomes}; okdec=any(x.get('type')=='boolean' for x in dec) or (any('approve' in o for o in onames) and any('reject' in o for o in onames)); assert okdec,'need boolean decision field or approve/reject outcomes'; rk=('reason','comment','explanation','justification','note'); assert any(x.get('direction') in ('output','inOut') and x.get('type') in ('text','string','textarea') and any(k in ft(x,'id') or k in ft(x,'label') for k in rk) for x in fields),'need a text reason output field'; assert any(e.get('sourceNodeId')==hid and e.get('sourcePort') in ('completed','outcome-completed') for e in edges),'HITL completed handle must be wired'; scripts=[str(n.get('inputs',{}).get('script','')) for n in nodes if n.get('type')=='core.action.script']; assert any((chr(36)+'vars.'+str(hid)+'.output') in s for s in scripts),'downstream script must read HITL output via vars.<hitl>.output'; print('OK')\""
    timeout: 15
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 6.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  # The project name is a WITHHELD, COSMETIC requirement (persona reveals it only
  # if asked what to name it) — the flow behaves identically whatever it's called.
  # Non-gating: reports whether the agent elicited the exact name (score 1/0), but
  # pass_threshold 0 keeps a cosmetic miss from failing the task and the low weight
  # keeps it from dominating the score.
  - type: run_command
    description: "Project/flow is named ExpenseApproval (elicited from the user)"
    command: "python3 -c \"import glob,sys; sys.exit(0 if glob.glob('**/ExpenseApproval.flow',recursive=True) else 'expected a flow named ExpenseApproval.flow')\""
    timeout: 15
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 1.0
    pass_threshold: 0
